The legal framework for prosecuting such acts draws on the Indian Penal Code (section 121 and related provisions), the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (1967) (section 15 defining “terrorist act”), and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (2023) (section 113 prescribing punishments for terrorist acts) [4
The Supreme Court identified Kasab’s primary crime as “conspiracy to wage war against India” [7].

This corresponds to the offence of *waging war* under Section 121 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) [4] (still in force post‑2024 as the IPC has been replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, but the IPC provision remains cited in case law).

The attacks also fall within the definition of a *terrorist act* under Section 15 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (1967) [1], which includes acts intended to strike terror, using explosives or firearms, causing death, injury, or damage to property.

1. **धारा 138 की सामग्री** – यह धारा कहती है कि यदि कोई व्यक्ति अपने खाते से जारी किया गया चेक, जो किसी ऋण या देनदारी के भुगतान के लिये है, बैंक द्वारा ‘अपर्याप्त निधियों’ या ‘अनुबंधित सीमा से अधिक’ कारणों से अस्वीकृत किया जाता है,

**Short answer**  
The punishment for murder in India is death or life imprisonment, and the offender is also liable to a fine. Under the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the same punishment applies, with an additional provision for group murders on specified grounds [4][9].  

**Analysis**  
- **Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC)** – Section 302 prescribes that “whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine” [1].  
- **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)** – Section 103 mirrors the IPC provision, stating that “whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine” [4].  
- T
